name: Full Factors Weighted (FFW) Importance Score Pruning
definition: A pruning method that computes an importance score for each Gaussian primitive using a combination of position, color, opacity, and transparency to selectively remove less important Gaussians while preserving visual quality.
summary: Full Factors Weighted Importance Score Pruning reduces memory and latency by ranking 3D Gaussians using position, color, and opacity factors, unlike methods relying solely on transparency.
